subject: seahorse
pitch: A lined seahorse holding on to a strand of seagrass with its curled tail. A ridged body in sunny yellow with thin dark lines and a few white freckles, a little crown of spikes on its head, a long tube snout, a delicate fluttering fin on its back, and big, curious eyes.

I'm sketching the body as a chain of joints from hips to neck, following a curved spine path, and considering how to render the ridged plating along the torso—maybe using stacked rings or lathe-style bands to get that textured seahorse look.

For the tail, I'm thinking a spiral chain that curls back and wraps around the seagrass, using the builder's chain and sweep functions with a spiral path helper. The seagrass itself I'm treating as a prop, possibly a tube geometry, since props don't need joints like the rest of the model.

Confirming the tail taper radii and checking the tube clears the blade's thickness with margin, then sketching the spine as a catmull path rising from the hips through the torso to a forward-leaning head joint near the top.

For color, I'm layering a base yellow with dark horizontal stripe bands (perpendicular to the y-axis, matching the natural rings on a seahorse body) and considering scattering lighter freckle spots on top, though combining stripe and spot paints together needs some care since they aren't trivially nestable.
